printed_headline_estimate: All WASH data are descriptive only (Tables 4-5, PDF pp. 10, 12; n = 428). Inferential tests (chi-square and Pearson r, n = 428) examine non-WASH outcomes only: post-conflict tenure -> housing construction quality satisfaction (chi2(24, n = 428) = 195.26, p < 0.001, PDF p. 8); post-conflict tenure -> perceived ability to self-isolate (chi2(24) = 94.0, p < 0.001; r = 0.26, p < 0.001, PDF p. 8); housing damage -> livelihood satisfaction (chi2(20) = 57.06, p < 0.001; r = -0.17, p < 0.001, PDF p. 6) and community safety (chi2(20) = 60.5, p < 0.001; r = -0.15, p = 0.001, PDF p. 6); poverty -> health service satisfaction (chi2(12) = 42.3, p < 0.001; r = -0.15, p = 0.001, PDF p. 13).
publication_year_note: Published in International Journal of Disaster Resilience in the Built Environment, Vol. 17 No. 2, 2026, pp. 297-313 (Received 23 June 2025; Revised 26 September 2025; Accepted 3 March 2026).
rationale: Although the household survey of 428 displaced households in Marawi collects both tenure/governance variables and household WASH conditions, every WASH measure (toilet access, sanitation system, drinking and washing water source, water treatment, handwashing in Table 4, PDF p. 10; satisfaction with drinking/washing water quantity and quality and solid waste management in Table 5, PDF p. 12) is reported purely as univariate descriptive percentages. The five inferential statistical tests (chi-square and Pearson correlation) reported in the paper test only non-WASH outcomes failing Criterion 4: post-conflict housing tenure vs. housing construction quality satisfaction (PDF p. 8) and vs. perceived ability to self-isolate from COVID-19 (PDF p. 8), housing conflict damage vs. livelihood satisfaction and community safety (PDF p. 6), and poverty status vs. general health service satisfaction (PDF p. 13). No inferential estimate links tenure, governance, or consultation to any water or sanitation service access outcome.
